c.tagline: A whitewashed Cycladic party island of windmills, Little Venice sunsets, and glamorous beach clubs

card: Widely accepted, including at beach clubs; cash useful for small tavernas
rides: Local taxi companies (very limited, book well ahead)

taxi.fare: Metered, though notoriously scarce in peak season
taxi.fareNote: Taxis are extremely limited; renting an ATV or booking a private transfer in advance is strongly recommended

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

english.label: Easy to get by in English

walk: Chora's old town is compact, car-free, and walkable; the island's beaches are spread out and require a bus, ATV, taxi, or boat

safety.safety: Very safe island, extremely crowded and expensive in peak summer
safety.crime: Petty theft in crowded nightlife areas is the main concern

hood_landmark.Chora (Mykonos Town): Little Venice's waterfront houses and the Kato Mili windmills
hood_landmark.Paradise Beach: Paradise Beach's famous beach clubs and party scene
hood_landmark.Platys Gialos: Platys Gialos's organized beach with water taxi connections
hood_landmark.Ano Mera: Ano Mera village's traditional, non-touristy square

avoid.reason: Watch for drink spiking and heavy overcharging at beach clubs, and pickpockets in Chora's packed lanes in high season.

hood_desc: The island's main town and nightlife hub, a maze of whitewashed lanes, boutiques, and the iconic Little Venice waterfront.
The island's most famous party beach, lined with beach clubs that transition from day lounging to all-night dancing.
A calmer, more sheltered beach south of Chora, popular with families and a good base for a quieter stay.
An organized beach with water taxi links to Paradise and Super Paradise, popular for its range of beachfront restaurants.
An inland village largely untouched by tourism, offering a glimpse of everyday Mykonian life away from the beach scene.
lodging: Santa Marina, a Luxury Collection Resort, Mykonos

water.note: Desalinated tap water is not recommended for drinking; buy bottled.

transit.sys: KTEL local bus network connecting Chora to the island's beaches
transit.note: Renting an ATV or booking private transfers is popular given the extreme scarcity of taxis in peak season

transport.air: Mykonos Island National Airport (JMK), about 15 min from Chora, with direct flights from Athens and seasonal international routes
transport.bus: KTEL buses connect the airport, Chora, and the main beaches
transport.ferry: Ferries connect to Athens (Piraeus), Santorini, and other Cycladic islands
transport.car: Rental cars and ATVs are popular; roads can be congested in peak season

airport.name: Mykonos Island National Airport
airport.transport: Taxi (book ahead), bus, or hotel shuttle

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A Cosmote or Vodafone Greece tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours

food.name: Kopanisti
food.desc: Mykonos' protected soft cheese, hand-kneaded and ripened until it turns peppery-sharp and almost spreadable. Eaten on rusks, or with tomato and capers.

places.name: Nikos Taverna
places.note: Long-standing Chora taverna near the old port; kopanisti and grilled fish at honest prices.

places.name: M-eating
places.note: Creative Mykonian cooking; kopanisti worked into modern plates, and the island's best melopita.

places.name: Kiki's Tavern
places.note: No electricity, no sign, charcoal grill only; free wine while you queue, cheese and salads to start.

food.name: Louza
food.desc: Pork loin cured with salt, pepper and savoury, then air-dried in the Aegean wind until translucent. Sliced paper-thin, often with local sausage alongside.

places.name: To Maereio
places.note: Tiny room, short Mykonian-only menu; the reference plate of louza and Mykonian sausage.

places.name: Captain's Restaurant
places.note: Waterfront classic by the pelicans; local cured meats and cheeses among the seafood.

places.name: Nikolas Taverna
places.note: Family taverna on the sand serving island cured meats before the grilled fish.

food.name: Kremmydopita
food.desc: Mykonian onion pie - sweet island onions slow-cooked with local cheese and mint inside a thin hand-rolled crust. A rustic, rarely exported specialty.

places.name: Fokos Taverna
places.note: Remote beach taverna, no sunbeds, no music; homemade pies and vegetables from the garden.

places.name: To Maereio
places.note: Cooks the old Mykonian household recipes; book, because there are only a handful of tables.

places.name: Kounelas Fish Tavern
places.note: Family fish taverna since the 1950s; savoury pies and mezze alongside the day's catch.

food.name: Kleftiko
food.desc: Lamb sealed with garlic, lemon and herbs and baked for hours until it collapses off the bone - named for the bandits who cooked it in buried pits.

places.name: Nikolas Taverna
places.note: Renowned for slow-baked lamb and a cosy beachside setting away from the party beaches.

places.name: Joanna's Nikos Place
places.note: Sunset-facing family taverna with authentic Greek cooking and generous portions.

places.name: Kiki's Tavern
places.note: Charcoal-cooked meats and big salads; expect a wait, it is worth it.

food.name: Melopita
food.desc: Mykonos honey-cheese pie: fresh unsalted island cheese whipped with thyme honey and eggs, baked in a thin shell and dusted with cinnamon.

places.name: M-eating
places.note: Widely reckoned to make the best melopita on the island; open late for post-dinner dessert.

places.name: To Maereio
places.note: Traditional home-style melopita to close a Mykonian tasting menu.

places.name: Fokos Taverna
places.note: Rustic melopita with local honey after a long lunch by an empty beach.

food.name: Amygdalota
food.desc: Soft almond sweets shaped into pears or ovals, scented with rosewater and rolled in icing sugar - the island's traditional wedding and festival treat.

places.name: Gioras Wood Medieval Bakery
places.note: Wood-fired bakery running since the 1420s; almond sweets and Mykonian rusks baked daily.

places.name: Ano Mera village bakeries
places.note: Inland village square where the bakeries still make amygdalota the old way, at village prices.

places.name: Matogianni Street sweet shops
places.note: Row of pastry shops on the main lane; buy them boxed as the standard island gift.

food.name: Rakomelo and souma
food.desc: Souma is the Cycladic pomace spirit distilled after the grape harvest; warmed with honey, cinnamon and cloves it becomes rakomelo.

places.name: To Maereio
places.note: Finishes the meal with a carafe of house souma; genuinely local rather than a tourist pour.

places.name: Fokos Taverna
places.note: Homemade rakomelo on a wind-blown terrace, far from the Chora crowds.

places.name: Nikolas Taverna
places.note: Complimentary digestif after dinner, the traditional Greek taverna sign-off.

food.name: Mykonian wine
food.desc: The island grows Assyrtiko, Mandilaria and old Cycladic varieties on low bush vines; crisp, saline whites and light reds built for seafood.

places.name: Vioma Organic Farm and Vineyard
places.note: Mykonos' organic working vineyard; tastings among the vines with meze from the farm.

places.name: M-eating
places.note: Strong all-Greek list with Mykonian and wider Cycladic bottles by the glass.

places.name: Bakalo
places.note: Grocer-style Greek restaurant with a well-chosen island wine selection and good mezze.

landmarks: Windmills of Kato Mili
Five whitewashed 16th-century windmills stand in an iconic row above the harbor, catching the same Aegean winds that once ground the island's grain.
Little Venice (Alefkandra)
Balconied captains' houses hang directly over the lapping sea, now packed with cocktail bars famous for the Aegean's most romantic sunsets.
Panagia Paraportiani
Four chapels fused over centuries into one sculptural whitewashed mass, this is among Greece's most photographed churches, glowing at the harbor's edge.
Delos Island
A short boat ride away lies the sacred birthplace of Apollo, a UNESCO-listed open-air museum of temples, mosaics, and the famous Naxian lions.
Chora (Mykonos Town) and Matogianni Street
A dazzling labyrinth of white lanes, bougainvillea, and chic boutiques designed to confuse pirates now delights fashionable wanderers instead.
Armenistis Lighthouse
This 1891 lighthouse on the island's windswept northwest cape offers dramatic cliff scenery and sunset views across to neighboring Tinos.
Panagia Tourliani Monastery, Ano Mera
A marble-towered 16th-century monastery with a dazzling carved iconostasis anchors the island's quieter inland village of Ano Mera.
Paradise Beach
The legendary golden crescent that made Mykonos a party capital still throbs with beach clubs, DJs, and turquoise water by day.
Elia Beach
The island's longest sandy beach unfurls beneath sculpted hills, offering sunbeds, calm water, and a more relaxed alternative to the party coves.
Archaeological Museum of Mykonos
Near the old port, this 1902 museum guards funerary treasures from nearby Rheneia and a celebrated 7th-century-BC pithos depicting the Trojan Horse.

train.note: There is no railway on Mykonos or in the Cyclades - Hellenic Train (https://www.hellenictrain.gr/en) serves only the Greek mainland, and Greece's international rail services are all suspended. Arrive by ferry or fly into Mykonos airport, which has seasonal direct flights from across Europe.

bus.note: No international or mainland coach routes exist from an island. KTEL Mykonos runs buses from the Fabrika and Old Port stations to Ornos, Platis Gialos, Paradise and Elia beaches and the New Port at Tourlos, running late into the night in summer. Buy tickets at the kiosks; the network shrinks considerably in winter.

intl.to: Santorini, Paros, Naxos & Ios (Greece) - high-speed catamaran

ferry.note: All sailings are domestic - there is no international route from Mykonos. Note that mainland ferries use two different Athens ports: Rafina is closer to the airport and often quicker, Piraeus is better connected to the city. Boats dock at the New Port at Tourlos, a couple of kilometres from Mykonos town, with a shuttle bus. Sailings are cancelled in strong meltemi winds through July and August.

half.name: Tinos
half.blurb: A Cycladic island famous for its marble dovecotes and the pilgrimage church of Panagia Evangelistria.

half.name: Naxos
half.blurb: The largest Cycladic island, with the marble Portara gate ruin, mountain villages, and Venetian-era architecture.

half.name: Paros
half.blurb: A whitewashed Cycladic island with the marble-columned Panagia Ekatontapiliani church and the harbor town of Naoussa.

half.name: Rhenia Island
half.blurb: An uninhabited island a short boat ride from Mykonos, with quiet coves and no facilities or crowds.
